doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Music business, his degree and the CD with Monk Rowe
summary: He says his business degree helps manage money and recalls the CD session with Watrous, Richardson and Betts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: The music business these days: there must be highs and lows throughout the year for you.
Yup. So thank God I have a business degree, and you just learn to manage your money and manage yourself and conduct yourself—
So there was some use in that thing there.

Some use there, just conduct yourself in a nice manner. But I’ve gotten to play with some of the greatest man. I mean that CD we did together, you had some of the greatest people on there — Bill Watrous, Jerome Richardson, Keter Betts, yourself.
Yeah, we had a really, really great time doing that. You did some really fantastic music.
